narratives.Description: Make `directive init` the universal adoption entrypoint: a dispatcher that classifies the current directory via the merged keystone plan()/classify() fact-set and transparently does the right thing. Empty dirs get scaffolded, brownfield dirs get Directive support without disturbing app code, an already-current install is delegated to `update` with a disclosure line, and a legacy/pre-cutover layout is routed to `migrate` -- always printing a state summary plus exactly one next action, and single-sourcing the logic by calling the narrow verbs rather than re-implementing them.
narratives.Overview:
Part of epic #2203. Absorbs #2198.

## Summary

Make `directive init` the **universal adoption entrypoint** — a dispatcher that classifies the directory (via the #child A fact-set) and does the right thing, so users never have to choose between `update`, `doctor`, `migrate`, or `migrate:xbrief` before their first command.

## Behavior (Decision 6 — dispatcher, not hidden-update)

`init` reads the fact-set/`plan()` result and **dispatches transparently**, always printing a state summary + exactly one action:

- Empty dir -> scaffold Directive (`.deft/core` projection, AGENTS.md managed section, xBRIEF layout, `package.json` pin).
- Brownfield (app code, no Directive) -> install Directive support without disturbing app code; point toward brownfield spec extraction + xBRIEF setup.
- Already initialized + current -> **delegate to `update`** with a disclosure line ("Existing current install detected — refreshing via `update`."). Never silently masquerade as update (that is the #2199 anti-pattern), never bounce the user to a second command.
- Legacy / pre-cutover -> **route to `migrate`** (the specific migration path), one clear next action.

Logic is single-sourced: init calls `update`/`migrate`; it does not re-implement them. CI/scripts that want predictability call the narrow verbs directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `init` handles empty, brownfield, already-initialized, stale, and legacy-layout dirs from any cwd.
- Prints a concise state summary + exactly one recommended next action.
- On an initialized-current project, delegates to `update` with disclosure — does not re-scaffold and does not silently refresh under the `init` name.
- Prefers `directive ...` over `task ...` for normal users.
- `--dry-run` / `--plan` prints the plan without executing.
- Idempotent.
- Tests cover the major project-state cases including brownfield+pre-cutover.

## Related

Absorbs #2198. Depends on #child A. Parent #2203.
narratives.UserStory: As a first-time Directive adopter in any directory state, I want `directive init` to classify my project via the shared plan() fact-set and transparently dispatch to scaffold or update or migrate while printing one clear next action, so that I never have to choose between init or update or doctor or migrate before my first command and init never silently masquerades as update.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add a new dispatcher module `packages/core/src/init-deposit/init-dispatch.ts` that consumes the merged keystone `classify()`/`plan()` from `packages/core/src/resolution/` (read-only) and maps the resolved mode to one of: scaffold (empty), brownfield-install, delegate-to-update (already-current), route-to-migrate (legacy/pre-cutover). Export it from `packages/core/src/init-deposit/index.ts`.
2. Single-source delegation: the dispatcher calls the existing `runRefreshDepositCli` (update, in refresh.ts) and `runMigrateCli` (migrate.ts) by import -- it MUST NOT re-implement or edit their logic. Always print a state summary + exactly one next action, and emit the disclosure line before delegating to update.
3. Rewire `packages/cli/src/init-cli/init.ts` so `directive init` calls the dispatcher instead of unconditionally running the greenfield deposit; keep the greenfield scaffold path for the empty/brownfield branches. Add `--dry-run`/`--plan` to `CANONICAL_INIT_ARGV` in `packages/cli/src/init-cli/constants.ts` (mirror UPDATE_DRY_RUN_FLAGS) and thread it through so the classified plan prints without executing.
4. Keep init idempotent and confined to the init surface: do NOT touch dispatch.ts (init routes via cli-router, already registered), doctor, xbrief-migrate, or README. Consume resolution/* read-only.
5. Colocated vitest in `init-dispatch.test.ts` + `init-cli.test.ts` + `init-deposit.test.ts` covering empty/brownfield/already-current/stale/legacy-pre-cutover from an arbitrary cwd, plus dry-run and idempotency. Add a brief CHANGELOG entry. Run `task ts:check-lane`, targeted vitest, and `task check:framework-source`.
